title: Bridge Runway: Stabilization Sprint Playbook for Multi-Region Degradations
author: Asha Nambiar
body:
Summary:
This playbook defines the 'Stabilization Sprint' pattern: a short, high-intensity incident flow used when a regional or multi-region degradation threatens SLOs but can be recovered via coordinated remediation and orchestration within a 2–6 hour window. It focuses on rapid containment, tactical rollouts, customer-safe messaging, and a structured handoff into post-incident workstreams.

When to use this playbook:
- Scope: region(s) or major capacity pool with measurable SLO drift (see "SLO thresholds" below).
- Use this instead of a full incident if recovery plausibly completes within a working-day sprint (<= 6 hours) and no P0 legal/compliance escalation is required.
- Not for silent data integrity or security incidents; use security/IR runbooks for those.

SLO thresholds (trigger conditions):
- Availability: region availability falls below 99.9% over the last 15m AND customer error-rate > 2x baseline for > 10m.
- Latency: p95 generation latency > 1s (hosted API) or p99 > 2s depending on model class.
- Throughput: sustained request queue growth > 30% above provisioned burst capacity for 15m.

Key roles and responsibilities:
- Bridge Conductor (owner): runs the stabilization sprint, keeps timeline, and owns customer/status messages.
- Tier-1 Responder (frontline): performs immediate diagnostics and mitigation actions (restart shards, clear KV cache, revert canary).
- Service Steward (domain expert): validates root cause hypotheses and approves fallbacks/rollouts.
- Capacity Lead: coordinates Dedicated and Private capacity moves, scaling, or capacity masking.
- Customer Liaison: prepares and publishes status messages and direct customer comms for impacted accounts.
- Incident Scribe: documents chronology and evidence in the incident dossier.

Pre-incident readiness checklist (bootstrap before sprint start):
- Verify bridge channel exists (bridge-call + dedicated slack #bridge-runway).
- Confirm runbook artifacts present: metric dashboards, alert symlinks, hotfix playbooks, and deployment rollbacks.
- Clear short-term quotas and ensure runbooks for eviction/queue flushing are accessible.
- Assign roles (names) and document in the bridge header.

Stabilization Sprint runbook (timeline and actions):
0-10 minutes — Triage & stabilization kickoff
1. Bridge Conductor starts the bridge, announces concise summary: scope, initial impact, SLOs at risk, and appointed roles.
2. Tier-1 Responder runs immediate containment actions: switch traffic to fallback model variants, disable background batch jobs, and apply circuit-breaker rules.
3. Customer Liaison posts initial status (internal and public status page short message) and flags high-touch customers for phone/SMS.

10-30 minutes — Evidence gathering & first mitigations
1. Collect top evidence: key traces, p95/p99 latency buckets, saturated GPUs, and queue depth snapshots. Capture JSON snippets from metrics collector.
2. Service Steward validates whether a hotfix can be applied (e.g., kernel parameter change, config flip, scaling policy adjustment).
3. Capacity Lead evaluates whether to add reserved nodes or redirect burst traffic between regions. If adding capacity, note expected warm-up time.

30-90 minutes — Tactical remediation and controlled rollout
1. Approve minimal-risk rollout path: canary on <5% of traffic, followed by 15m bake windows.
2. If rollback is needed, use the documented rollback command set (see Appendix).
3. Monitor impact windows closely (every 5 minutes). Update bridge every 10 minutes.

90-240 minutes — Recovery & stabilization sprint closure criteria
1. Recovery indicators: availability >= target SLO for 15m, p95 latency within normal bounds, and queue depth decreasing.
2. If stable, announce phased closure: shift bridge to monitoring-only mode and plan handoff to remediation backlog.
3. If not stabilizing, escalate to a sustained incident path with exec notification.

Customer communications: status page templates and direct messaging
- Public short status (initial):
  "Short: We are investigating increased latency for requests in <region>. Some customers may experience slower responses. Our engineers are actively working on a mitigation. Updates every 15 minutes."
- Public update (after tactical mitigation):
  "Update: We applied a targeted mitigation that reduced error rates and latency by ~40% for affected requests. We continue to monitor; targeted customers will receive direct updates as needed."
- Customer high-touch email template (concise, customer-facing):
  Subject: Service impact in <region> — update
  Body: Hello <Customer>, we observed elevated latency and errors affecting requests routed to <region>. Our team implemented a mitigation at <time UTC> which restored majority traffic path performance. We are monitoring and will follow up with a full post-incident report. If you need immediate assistance, reply to this message or contact <CS-Pager>.

Status page guidance:
- Use the unified status page with these fields: incident_id, short_description, impact, start_time, current_status, next_update ETA. Keep public messages high-level and avoid speculative root causes.

Decision checklist (for rolling changes during stabilization):
- Is the change reversible within the bake window?
- Does the change reduce customer-impacting errors in canary?
- Is the change's blast radius scoped to a known tenant set or region?
- Has Service Steward approved? If no, delay change and continue mitigations.

Escalation rules:
- If SLOs not trending back within 2 hours, escalate to Executive War Room and add PM/CS leads.
- Any sign of data loss or incorrect outputs must immediately trigger the Security & Compliance incident path.

Post-sprint handoff and postmortem process:
- If stabilized: the Bridge Conductor opens a postmortem ticket in the incident board, assigns triage owners, and schedules a 48–72h follow-up retro.
- Minimum artifacts for postmortem: incident timeline, key metrics (time series snapshots), failed runbook actions, and the customer communication log.
- Postmortem rubric (must include): summary, timeline, root cause hypothesis, corrective actions (owner+ETA), and prevention steps.

Game day & rehearsal plan (quarterly):
- Objective: validate the Stabilization Sprint flow end-to-end with a simulated regional degradation.
- Participants: Bridge Conductor, Tier-1 Responder, Service Steward, Capacity Lead, Customer Liaison, Scribe.
- Scenarios: saturated GPU cluster, KV cache eviction storm, model rollout causing p99 spikes.
- Success metrics: bridge established in <=5 minutes, first mitigation applied in <=15 minutes, canary and rollback exercised, customer message published within 10 minutes.
- Post-exercise deliverables: short retro, runbook updates, and a list of actionable improvements assigned in sprint backlog.

Appendix: useful commands and snippets
- Rollback example (deployment): kubectl -n inference rollout undo deployment/model-service --to-revision=<rev>
- Cache flush (service CLI): redwood-cli cache flush --service model-service --region <region> --prefix kv-prefix
- Query (metrics): curl -s "https://metrics.internal/api/query?expr=llm_request_p95{region=\"<region>\"}&start=<t0>&end=<t1>" | jq .

Audit and evidence collection checklist:
- Save raw traces and span IDs for 30 days (attach to incident ticket).
- Export the dashboard snapshots and upload PNGs to the incident dossier.
- Confirm which customer buckets were impacted and preserve request IDs for customer reconciliation.

Related known runbooks and pages:
- Include links to per-service hotfix runbooks, retro templates, and the status page playbook.

Maintenance and ownership:
- The Bridge Runway playbook is owned by Eng SRE. Review cadence: annual review + after every stabilization sprint.
- Contact for updates: eng-sre-runbooks@redwood.ai

Last reviewed by: Marcus Lee, Jillian Park, Tomás Ortega
